skill.name: backend-queries

skill.summary: Improve backend database queries for security, performance, and maintainability.

content.value_statement: Backend code often ships slow or unsafe queries. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code toward parameterized, indexed, and transaction-aware database access.
actual_capabilities: Guides use of parameterized queries for safer SQL handling.
Prompts eager loading to reduce N+1 query problems.
Encourages selecting only needed columns instead of broad result sets.
Covers filtering, sorting, pagination, joins, subqueries, and aggregations.
Calls for transactions around related database operations.
Highlights indexing, caching, query timeouts, and slow query debugging.
limitations: Provides guidance only and does not execute database analysis.
Requires the user to provide project framework and ORM context.
Does not include database-specific migration or schema generation steps.
References a detailed standards file outside the packaged skill.

use_cases.title: Secure Controller Queries
use_cases.description: Help application developers write safer query logic inside controllers, services, repositories, and model methods.

use_cases.title: Performance Review
use_cases.description: Help technical leads review query patterns for eager loading, indexing, pagination, and result size control.

use_cases.title: Transaction Planning
use_cases.description: Help platform engineers design consistent transaction boundaries for related database writes and rollback handling.

prompt_templates.title: Review A Simple Query
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review of one backend query.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this backend query for safety and performance. Focus on parameterization, selected columns, and basic indexing needs.

prompt_templates.title: Fix N Plus One Issues
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze this ORM code for N+1 query risks. Suggest eager loading changes and explain the expected database behavior.

prompt_templates.title: Design Filtered Pagination
prompt_templates.prompt: Design query logic for filtering, sorting, and pagination. Include safe parameter handling, stable ordering, and index recommendations.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Complex Transactions
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this multi-step database workflow. Define transaction boundaries, rollback behavior, timeout handling, and query performance risks.

output_examples.input: Review a repository method that builds user filters and sorting.
output_examples.output: The response identifies unsafe dynamic sorting, recommends allowlisted sort fields, and suggests an index for common filter columns.

output_examples.input: Improve a service that loads orders and order items.
output_examples.output: The response explains the N+1 risk, recommends eager loading, and describes how to limit selected fields.

output_examples.input: Plan a checkout workflow that writes several records.
output_examples.output: The response defines transaction scope, rollback conditions, timeout concerns, and query checks for inventory consistency.

best_practices: Provide the ORM, database engine, and relevant model relationships before asking for query changes.
Ask for security and performance review together when queries accept user input.
Request index guidance when adding filters, joins, sorting, or pagination.
anti_patterns: Do not ask for raw SQL concatenation with user-controlled values.
Do not use broad result selection when only a few columns are needed.
Do not skip transaction planning for related writes that must succeed together.

faq.question: Can this skill write database queries from scratch?
faq.answer: Yes. It can guide new query logic when you provide models, relationships, and expected behavior.

faq.question: Does it support both ORM and raw SQL work?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers query builders, ORM methods, joins, subqueries, aggregations, and raw SQL security concerns.

faq.question: Can it detect N+1 query problems?
faq.answer: It can review code for N+1 patterns and recommend eager loading or batching approaches.

faq.question: Does it run queries against my database?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance and review, but it does not connect to or inspect a live database.

faq.question: What context should I provide?
faq.answer: Provide the database engine, ORM or query builder, model relationships, current query code, and performance goals.

faq.question: Is the skill ready for marketplace packaging?
faq.answer: It needs the external standards reference moved inside the skill package before publication.
